name: Hoffman Estates
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Hoffman Estates, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Hoffman Estates, IL: free Winterfest sleigh rides, Skate with Santa, free Santa photos at Cabela's and a kids Pajama Jam night.
lede: Hoffman Estates lights its Friendship Tree outside Village Hall the Saturday before Thanksgiving, with fireworks and Santa. December brings the park district's free Winterfest with sleigh rides, Skate with Santa at the Triphahn Center and free Santa photos at Cabela's.
celebrates: The season in Hoffman Estates starts at Village Hall on Hassell Road with the Friendship Tree Lighting Ceremony, held the Saturday before Thanksgiving. The mayor and a Cub Scout troop light the tree, fireworks follow, and families then head inside for visits with Santa, songs from the Choral-Aires and light refreshments. In early December the Hoffman Estates Park District hosts Winterfest at the Bridges of Poplar Creek Country Club, with horse-drawn sleigh rides, ice-less skating and s'mores, plus a ticketed Breakfast with Santa. Santa also skates at the Triphahn Center and poses for free photos at Cabela's on Prairie Stone Parkway.
lastyear: In 2025 the Friendship Tree Lighting Ceremony was planned for Saturday, November 22, at 5 pm in front of Village Hall, according to the village. The park district's Winterfest was planned for Saturday, December 6, 2025, from 10 am to 1:30 pm at the Bridges of Poplar Creek Country Club, with cocoa by the fire, games, rides and a new Tree Trail by John's Evergreens. A Breakfast with Santa was planned for that morning, with two seatings, at 8:30 and 11 am, priced at $30.95 for adults and $19.95 for children 4 to 12.
facts: The Friendship Tree is a large, living pine tree that grows outside Village Hall, and each year it is dressed in lights and more than 700 red bows. The village says the growing tree is a reminder of the community's commitment to friendship and the environment. Families can bring non-perishable food and personal care items to the lighting for local food pantries. The visitor bureau calls the fireworks after the lighting a unique experience during the winter. At Winterfest in 2024, mushers ran sled dog demonstrations and families could adopt a sled dog.
trains: Hoffman Estates families can board Metra at the Schaumburg station, 2000 S. Springinsguth Road, on the Milwaukee District West line. Metra's decorated Holiday Trains run on six lines in 2026, including the UP Northwest Line on December 12. For a Santa ride, the Fox River Trolley Museum in South Elgin runs Santa's Trolley Express on a decorated 1950s trolley, with hot chocolate, a story from Mrs. Claus and a visit from Santa. The Illinois Railway Museum in Union runs the Happy Holiday Railway, a train ride with Santa and his elves through the winter countryside.

faq: When is the Hoffman Estates tree lighting?

The village holds its Friendship Tree Lighting Ceremony on the Saturday before Thanksgiving each year, in front of the main entrance of Village Hall at 1900 Hassell Road. The mayor and a Cub Scout troop light the tree, a fireworks display follows, and families go inside for Santa, music and refreshments.
Is the Friendship Tree Lighting free?

Yes. The village describes the Friendship Tree Lighting as a free, family-friendly event. It fills up quickly, so the village suggests arriving early for a good view of the tree and the fireworks. Guests are invited to bring non-perishable food or personal care items for local food pantries.
What is Winterfest in Hoffman Estates?

Winterfest is the Hoffman Estates Park District's free winter celebration at the Bridges of Poplar Creek Country Club on Poplar Creek Drive. It mixes indoor and outdoor activities, such as horse-drawn sleigh rides, ice-less skating, a kids' craft station, s'mores and game tables, along with local vendors.
Where can kids see Santa in Hoffman Estates?

Santa appears at the Friendship Tree Lighting inside Village Hall, skates at the Triphahn Center and Ice Arena during the park district's Skate with Santa, and sits for free photos at Santa's Wonderland inside Cabela's on Prairie Stone Parkway, where Santa and Mrs. Claus also read stories on Tuesday evenings.
Why is it called the Friendship Tree?

The village says the large, living pine tree outside Village Hall serves as a reminder of the community's continuing commitment to friendship and the environment. Because the tree is still growing, Hoffman Estates decorates the same tree each year with lights and more than 700 red bows.
